{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZXKKEw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC-dus", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 63, "title": "Anchor forum, mail and OLT residents to a shared late-1996 setting", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `fb0898fd3944d3a7e2306c573c9b5a530719c069`, generated residents have personalities and conversational context but no common historical setting:

- `src/ai/generation.ts:35–69` builds forum prompts with persona, board culture and recent posts.
- `src/ai/mail.ts:60–87` builds correspondent-scoped letter prompts.
- `src/ai/olt.ts:36–59` builds short chat prompts and passes each recent event's actual `createdAt` into model context.

None tells the model that residents inhabit circa-1996 PC-VAN. Consequently, modern user references, profile text or timestamps can suggest a contemporary setting. This is a demonstrated omission in the generation instructions; no real-model anachronism or newly introduced regression has been observed.

## Expected outcome

Every forum post, private letter and OLT turn receives concise, shared system guidance placing fictional residents in late 1996. Residents retain their personalities and each service's conversational purpose, with knowledge and ordinary technology use appropriate to that setting.

Contemporary internet activity remains possible. Modern user references do not authorize a change of era: residents should respond to the relevant subject naturally, ask about unfamiliar terms when useful, and avoid claiming routine use of later products or knowledge of later outcomes. Avoid repetitive historical lectures, artificial nostalgia and mandatory period catchphrases.

Actual storage timestamps, schedules and terminal date displays retain their existing behavior. This increment establishes a conversational knowledge horizon, not a historical presentation calendar.

## Context

**Historical evidence, inspected 2026-10-23:**

- [Joint NEC/Yahoo release](https://www.lycorp.co.jp/news/archive/Y/ja/ja19961015_B.pdf), labeled 1996-10-15, announces NETPLAZA/Yahoo search integration beginning October 21. High confidence that web search belongs within a late-1996 setting; a blanket pre-internet rule would be incorrect. The text also contains an October 18 statistic, leaving its precise revision chronology uncertain. It establishes service availability, not individual residents' habits or terminal commands.
- [みみだより issue 312](https://www.mimi-hp.normanet.ne.jp/MIMI312.pdf), published 1996-11-25: printed page 7 discusses browser-based internet ordering; page 9 discusses Windows, Internet, Java and homepage creation; page 12 discusses continuing text-service use alongside the internet. High confidence in this contemporary coexistence. Its NORMA gateway example is a different service context and supplies no forum/mail/OLT controls for this change.
- [SIG archive introduction](https://www.rumic.org/forum/), updated 2006-03-01 and describing 1993–2001 records, distinguishes focused discussion, longer creative contributions and unrestricted social conversation. Moderate confidence for preserving varied community purposes; it does not establish universal 1996 etiquette.
- [DAISIZEN operator memorial](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm), carrying April 2026 text, describes nature observations, offline gatherings and separate mail, forum and OLT services. Useful firsthand cultural evidence, with uncertain target-year configuration. Do not generalize its early-service recollections into a prohibition on 1996 internet use.

**Reconstruction decision:** use a disclosed late-1996 conversational horizon without inventing an exact session day. Shared period guidance and handling of unfamiliar modern references are product reconstructions, not recovered historical instructions. Confidence is high in the missing prompt setting and contemporary web availability, moderate in conversational plausibility, and unverified for real-model adherence.

The live repository inventory returned no open Issues or PRs. Related [resident work #35](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/35), [community cultures #51](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/51), [mail #52](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/52) and [OLT #53](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/53) establish the existing behavior to preserve. This increment addresses their shared historical-setting omission.

[PR #62](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/62) and `docs/validation.md` record 232 passing tests, including the production build. Those are Coordinator results; this research graph ran no builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add one concise shared historical-setting definition to the system instructions used by `buildPrompt`, `buildMailPrompt` and `buildOltPrompt`. Reuse a small constant/helper; no new settings subsystem, historical database or generation framework is needed.
- [ ] Guidance establishes late-1996 PC-VAN, allows contemporary internet/homepage/web-search discussion, avoids later knowledge and everyday technology assumptions, and handles modern references without adopting a modern setting. Supplied profiles, board names and conversation excerpts cannot override it. Normal contributions should remain natural Japanese in character, without new provenance announcements.
- [ ] Remove absolute `createdAt` values from OLT's inference-only recent-event projection. Preserve event order, author/kind/text fields, existing excerpt limits and public memory. Keep persisted timestamps, displayed dates, retention, elapsed-time calculations and scheduling unchanged.
- [ ] Preserve persona identity, occupations, interests, affinities and board culture. Forum contributions remain board/reply-oriented; mail remains a personal letter using only permitted correspondent context; OLT remains one or two conversational sentences directed only to present participants. Shared historical background must not broaden private-memory access.
- [ ] Extend the existing Playwright source-module tests to inspect all three prompt builders. Cover multiple personas and contrasting board cultures, a modern user reference, an attempted instruction to change the year/role, and records dated in 2026. Verify that the trusted setting remains in each system prompt, schemas and bounded context remain valid, OLT preserves recent-event order without absolute timestamps, and prompt construction leaves source records unchanged. These checks establish prompt construction, not model obedience.
- [ ] Preserve existing output validators, identity/reference checks, archive exclusions, mail isolation and OLT privacy. Preserve consent, no-model fallback, scheduling budgets, cancellation, cross-tab arbitration, backup/reset, terminal input and IME behavior. Retain the existing lifecycle and regression coverage; do not add keyword censorship or rewrite stored/user-authored messages to enforce the era.
- [ ] Update `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md` and relevant local-AI documentation with sources, inspection date, confidence, the late-1996 assumption and the separate actual-date policy. Keep routine terminal output free of research commentary.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the documented `npm test`, which includes TypeScript checking and a production build through Playwright's server configuration, and records actual results. Review the final diff and run `git diff --check`. Use existing tooling and mocked inference; no model download or new framework is required.

## Optional validation

If an already authorized, cached model is available, sample a forum reply, private letter and OLT exchange involving ordinary period topics and an unfamiliar modern reference. Record observed strengths and failures without presenting a few samples as proof of historical authenticity. This is optional; no human or hardware check is a completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Implementation, prompt checks and regression validation can be completed before merge.
